A residual fusion `h_fused = h_sasrec + α·branch(pool)` preserves the original features and scores exactly at α=0, provided the original backbone and scorer remain unchanged and the branch produces finite values. A learnable scalar initialized to zero follows [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887); sigmoid gates with finite bias cannot equal zero exactly. Additional LayerNorm belongs inside the gated branch: `h + α·LN(project(pool))`. Applying a new LayerNorm after fusion changes the baseline even at zero gate. These are design deductions from the residual identity, not evidence of SASRec validation gains.

The [original SASRec implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py) scales input item embeddings by √d, leaves scoring embeddings unscaled, and applies final normalization to backbone features. Preserve those conventions; explicitly ablate raw versus √d-scaled pooled embeddings because branch magnitude controls the gate’s effective strength. During per-position training, pooling must use only nonpadding items at positions j≤t, optionally restricted to a recent window. Normalize weights over valid positions and return zero for empty prefixes. A sequence-wide recent pool broadcast across training positions leaks future interactions. Keep backbone masks unchanged when testing fusion alone; evaluate mask corrections separately.

Useful proposed controls: unchanged SASRec; SASRec plus the last observed item embedding; plus a uniform recent-window mean; plus an exponentially recency-weighted mean; then learned pooling with the same residual gate. Also compare standalone last-item and recency-weighted scorers. Hold embedding scale, projection, branch normalization and validation protocol constant across pooling comparisons. Verify zero-gate feature/logit equality in evaluation mode, padding invariance, and absence of future-token influence. The cited sources establish implementation principles, not superiority of these pooling variants; select using the four-category macro validation HR@10.
